newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain will join EMU despite debt - Treasury's Caruana.
newsitem.headline: Spain will join EMU despite debt - Treasury's Caruana.

text.p: Treasury director Jaime Caruana said Spain would join Europe's common currency launch although its debt to gross domestic product level would exceed 60 percent, according to a newspaper interview published on Friday.

"We aren't going to be below 60 percent in 1997. That much is clear. But debt will begin to trend lower next year and that is very important and means we will meet the criterion," Caruana told financial daily Gaceta de los Negocios.
The Maastricht Treaty, which sets forth the requirements for participation in the common currency, targets the debt ratio at a maximum 60 percent or declining.
But Caruana said Spain would meet the target ratio for budget deficit to gross domestic product, of three percent.
"The three percent gross domestic product (goal) will be met," Caruana said.
There are hopeful signs ahead for the budget deficit, which has fallen nine percent through the end of August compared with 1995, he added.

"There are a series of factors that give more hape for the next months. Interest payments on the debt have a non-lineal payment profile and for the first eight months of the year they rose 17 percent. At the end of the year, these interest payments will only have risen 17 percent," Caruana said.
He said that Spain was moving in the right direction on inflation thanks to the Bank of Spain's monetary policy which is focused on price stability.
